findings.title: NPE when the "Clients" resource-type resource does not exist
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` the code falls back to the resource-type resource: `resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE);` and then immediately calls `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource)`. `getResourceTypeResource()` returns `null` in several realistic cases: the realm does not have admin permissions enabled (but an admin-permissions client still exists from a previous activation), or the `Clients` resource was never created for that resource server (e.g. realms whose admin permissions client was initialized before this resource type existed). The result is a NullPointerException (HTTP 500) on every client admin REST call that evaluates a client permission instead of simply returning `false`. A null check is needed before the policy lookup (and before the subsequent `resource.getScopes()` call).

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission() cannot return individual clients and returns the literal "Clients" name
findings.body: `getClientsWithPermission(scope)` collects resources via `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and adds `resource.getName()` to the result set. However, the per-client resources created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource()` are created with `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner)` and never get a `type` assigned, so `findByType(..., "Clients", ...)` matches only the single resource-type resource whose name is `"Clients"`. Consequently this method (a) never returns the ids of clients that have an individual permission, and (b) returns the bogus entry `"Clients"` when an all-clients permission is granted. Callers treat the returned strings as client identifiers, so client filtering/listing based on this method is wrong in both directions.

findings.title: Client removal fails with UnsupportedOperationException when V1 and V2 fine-grained authz are both enabled
findings.body: The `ClientRemovedEvent` branch calls `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)`. `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled, and `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled()` throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. Since the new guard only checks `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1), a deployment with both features enabled will throw on every client deletion, failing the delete with a server error. The listener should resolve the V1 management implementation explicitly (or skip when V2 is active).

findings.title: V1-only entry points now throw UnsupportedOperationException and surface as HTTP 500
findings.body: `canExchangeTo()`, `isPermissionsEnabled()`, `getPermissions()` and `resource()` throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. These are still reachable while `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled: the token-exchange code path calls `clients().canExchangeTo(...)` when the V1 feature is enabled, and the admin endpoint `/admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions` calls `isPermissionsEnabled()`/`getPermissions()` unconditionally. With V2 enabled these calls now produce an uncaught runtime exception (HTTP 500) instead of a meaningful 400/404 response, and token exchange breaks outright when both features are enabled.

findings.title: New schema scopes are not created for already-initialized admin permission clients
findings.body: `init()` creates the authorization scopes from the schema only when the admin permissions client does not yet exist (it returns early otherwise). Adding `configure`, `map-roles-client-scope` and `map-roles-composite` to the schema therefore leaves realms whose admin-permissions client was already initialized without those scopes. In that state `getOrCreateResource()` throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` when creating a resource for a Clients permission (line 108), and creating any client permission with the new scopes fails with a validation error from `getScope()`. A migration/upgrade step that adds missing schema scopes (and the new `Clients` resource) to existing resource servers is required.

findings.title: getResourceName() has no handling for the new Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName()` resolves friendly names only for the `Users` resource type ("All users" / username). For the newly added `Clients` resource type it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is `null` for resources created by `getOrCreateResource()` (only name and owner are set). As a result, permissions created for clients expose a null/empty resource name through the admin API (and in the console), unlike user permissions; the name should be resolved to the client's clientId, with `"All clients"` for the resource-type resource.

findings.title: V1 permission cleanup is now skipped when the V1 feature is disabled
findings.body: Wrapping the whole listener body in `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` means that when the V1 feature is turned off, removal of roles, clients and groups no longer disables/cleans up their V1 fine-grained permission policies. Data created while the feature was enabled (policies/resources referencing the removed role/client/group) is left behind as orphaned authorization objects, which can resurface or break if the feature is re-enabled.

findings.title: Javadoc for requireView()/requireViewClientScopes() describes a return value instead of the thrown exception
findings.body: `requireView()` is documented as "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}." and `requireViewClientScopes()` as "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canViewClientScopes()} returns {@code true}." Both methods are `void` and throw `ForbiddenException` when the corresponding `can*` check fails, like the other `require*` methods documented in this file. The documentation is misleading for implementers/callers of this SPI-like interface and should state the ForbiddenException behaviour.

findings.title: Dead code left in new class
findings.body: `ClientPermissionsV2` contains a private, never-called `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` method (it was only needed for token exchange, which now throws `UnsupportedOperationException`), an unused `logger` field (line 51), and unused imports (`Scope`, `ClientModelIdentity`/`DefaultEvaluationContext` only used by the dead method, and the static import of `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE`). This dead code suggests an incomplete copy from `ClientPermissions` and should be removed to avoid confusion about whether token exchange is supported here.

findings.title: No test coverage for the map-roles-client-scope scope and client-scope level permissions
findings.body: The PR adds `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` to the Clients resource type and implements `canMapClientScopeRoles()`, `canManage(ClientScopeModel)`/`canView(ClientScopeModel)` and `getClientsWithPermission()` in `ClientPermissionsV2`, but the new tests only exercise `manage`, `configure`, `view`, `map-roles` and `map-roles-composite`. The scope-to-client-scope mapping path and the client-scope evaluators are therefore untested, which is where the issues above (e.g. `getClientsWithPermission` returning the resource-type name) would have been caught.
